item.title: This is my favorite tale of all time
item.content:encoded: Takes a somewhat 1 bit character and classic of the wiki and adds great info to it, that's both well written and works with the rest of the universe. item.content:encoded:
"SCP-058 - Heart of Darkness" is mentioned a few times in the article:

09/15/74 - SCP-058 breaches containment and enters the Safe-class biological containment sector, and proceeds to breach the attached research facility. Containment of SCP-███, ████, and ████ are damaged, and SCP-███ and -████ are destroyed. The south wall of SCP-682’s unit is damaged. Before further damage is done, SCP-1158 breaches containment nearby and floats down the hall, entangling SCP-058 in its tentacles. SCP-058 slows and appears to convulse, demonstrating a previously unknown sensitivity to SCP-1158's neurotoxin. 058 is later contained by site security, and 682 does not breach containment.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So...
my head is racing.

Funny how in this time line instead of active adaptation and use of its reality bending to preserve itself, it's just straight up active causation and probability manipulation that keep it from getting canned.

Ours must see humans as its big mistake, but is unable to affect anything other than itself substantially in the same way it created everything else. And then the Foundation gives it little windows back into the driver's seat.

By our cross testing to attempt to terminate it, 682 is able to hop along with the resulting effects and either ride it out as an additional phenomenon or suss the abilities of the anomalies as it remembers them and actively alter itself to render the threats null and preserve it's universe.

And all the while it wants to destroy Humanity because we turned out wrong compared to what it intended, we're disgusting to it. It can't fix what's already done, but it can at least wipe us out and ride along for a second loop in the future, possibly?

This is a 2760° that throws everything in inverse reverse forward, and I love how the newest entry in the termination log makes this shit even more cannon.

And dammit I'm toot tired to be crafting theories involving our glorious abusive lizard elder father, but I done did it. Even went to my sandbox to scrounge up proper collapsible format.
You're welcome, sleep tight, punch some sharks tonight.

item.content:encoded:
This remains one of my favorite entries for the contest. It might actually be my favorite. :3

Not just because of every other praise it's gotten so far (all of them well-deserved), but because of the image of a small bubble of space-time that survives by drifting outside everything else, apart, aside, away, connected to as many places as possible and extracting infinite tiny particulates of energy from infinite universes… and then coding their messages in the Big Bang.

In every Big Bang.

Seriously, there are so many levels of awesome in these notions that I cannot express them in words.

… and you continued to make use of Kiryu Labs. Kiryu Labs are awesome. Every time. :D
